Embeds utils.AuthorReachCapWhere, the most widely reused WHERE fragment in the codebase: JSON extraction plus haversine trigonometry plus spatial predicates. Named in plan 7.5. Note that reachcap.go itself builds a string and never executes it, so the cost lands on the callers that splice it in.

Migration harness. These sites execute the original raw SQL by design, in order to compare it against the replacement ORM call, so they are not migration targets.
Builds a SQLite export file, not a query against the Percona cluster. Out of scope for the MySQL-to-ORM work and unaffected by the engine migration.

Carries an optimiser hint, /*+ MAX_EXECUTION_TIME(10000) */, over messages_likes (~75M rows, and unindexed for this access pattern). The caller inspects .Error to set a degraded flag when the hint aborts a slow query, so the hint is load-bearing behaviour rather than a comment. It could probably be smuggled into the Select string, since GORM renders SELECT <select-clause> FROM, but getting that subtly wrong on a table this size degrades a live endpoint rather than failing visibly, so it wants a deliberate decision and its own test rather than a wave conversion.

The dump pipeline threads a raw *sql.DB rather than a *gorm.DB through buildDump/buildPlan/scanIDs/runDBSpec, and two of its four query sites build dynamic SQL text that was never extracted. Converting the other two would split one pipeline's connection handling across two patterns and needs a signature change, which is a redesign rather than a conversion. Consistent with the existing userdump/sqlite.go entry.
Layer 3 harness infrastructure. Reads the shadow batch flag from the config table by design and is not a migration target, in the same way the ormharness package is not.

The SELECT ... FOR UPDATE runs through tx.QueryRow on a raw *sql.Tx taken from db.DB().Begin(), and shares that transaction with a following raw INSERT that needs sql.Result.LastInsertId() on the same connection. Converting only the SELECT would either take it outside the transaction, defeating the row lock, or force the whole function onto db.Transaction(). Same shape as tryst.CreateTryst: a per-site redesign, not a mechanical conversion. Found during the Wave 1 chat batch.

INSERT whose caller needs LastInsertId from the exact connection that ran it. See the shared note on CreatePartnerUser below: GORM's map-valued Create writes the new id back under the literal key "@id" when no schema is parsed, which is undocumented, contradicts GORM's own 'Create From Map' documentation, and has no coverage in GORM's test suite. Found by the Wave 2 write pilot.

INSERT whose caller needs LastInsertId. These sites use sqlDB.Exec deliberately so the id is read from the MySQL protocol response on the very connection that performed the insert. The hazard being avoided is NOT replication lag: LAST_INSERT_ID() is connection-scoped session state, so a follow-up SELECT can be handed a different pooled connection and return 0 or another session's id, as the comment in session/social_auth.go already spells out. Converting to GORM's Create would instead depend on primary-key writeback that, traced through callbacks/create.go in v1.31.0, stores the id under the literal key "@id" when stmt.Schema is nil - real behaviour, but undocumented, contradicted by the public docs, and untested upstream. Relying on that for the one value these sites exist to protect is precisely the silent, expensive rewrite bug plan 7.5 reserves keep-raw for. database/insert.go's ExecInsertGetID already encapsulates this pattern and is itself recorded as non-migration infrastructure; pointing these call sites at it would be a sensible dedup, but that is a refactor rather than an ORM conversion.
INSERT whose caller needs LastInsertId; see the note on CreatePartnerUser. Found by the Wave 2 write pilot.

Deliberately drops to the database/sql handle so that LastInsertId() reports the row the upsert actually touched, and returns it to the caller. GORM's Create does not surface LastInsertId for an ON DUPLICATE KEY UPDATE, and the read/write split makes reading the id back with a follow-up SELECT unsafe. Found during the Wave 0 pilot; needs a per-site redesign rather than a mechanical conversion.
Infrastructure wrapper: takes an already-built statement from a caller and retries it. The SQL belongs to the calling site, which is inventoried separately.
Infrastructure wrapper around LAST_INSERT_ID handling for the read/write split. The SQL belongs to the calling site, which is inventoried separately.

PostTeam() inserts into teams and then reads the generated id back with LastInsertId() on the same connection. LAST_INSERT_ID() is connection-scoped session state, so the read is only correct while it shares a connection with the write. Converting this would move the id onto GORM map-Create's undocumented "@id" writeback and hand the connection choice to the dbresolver plugin. The failure mode is not an error: it is a row created against the wrong parent id, found days later. Enforced by ratchet gate (k); see tools/orm-migration/lastinsertid-sites.json.

INSERT ... SELECT: PostModConfig copies the bulkops rows of the template config into the new one in a single statement. GORM has no builder that expresses INSERT ... SELECT as one atomic statement - Create takes values, not a query - so converting it would mean reading the rows and inserting them separately, which is a different statement with a different concurrency story, not a port. No INSERT ... SELECT site anywhere in the manifest has been converted; they are all still raw. Note this is NOT a LastInsertId site: an earlier version of check-lastinsertid.sh flagged it by proximity, because the LastInsertId in this function belongs to the mod_configs INSERT below it, not to this one.

INSERT ... SELECT: copies the message attachment rows into the newsfeed post in one statement. GORM has no builder that keeps INSERT ... SELECT atomic - Create takes values, not a query - so a conversion would become a read followed by a separate insert, which is a different statement with a different concurrency story. No INSERT ... SELECT site anywhere in the manifest has been converted.

Dynamic SQL (manifest records dynamic: true). The position value is assembled with fmt.Sprintf, embedding lng, lat and the SRID as literal text into the statement before it is ever executed, so the recorded goldenSql is the pre-format Go source text rather than SQL. There is nothing a GORM render could be compared against, which makes Layer 1 parity impossible for this site by construction rather than by difficulty. Plan 7.4 requires a passing parity test before a site counts as converted, so it stays raw.
